issue.title: test_commit_publication_drain_accounting.py fails run alone: scanner-timeout test's blanket require_rust_binding patch poisons git_lock_facade
issue.description:
Proposed by sase-1tz.2.1.6 note #3. The same failure was also reported by sase-1tz.2.1.2 note #3, sase-1tz.2.1.3 note #3, sase-1tz.2.1.8 note #2 and sase-1tz.2.1.9 note #2, and earlier by sase-1qt.2 notes #2-#3. The sase-1tz.2.1 land agent triaged it on master fb85972f27 (2026-11-20).

## Reproduction (deterministic)

    .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/agents_sync/test_commit_publication_drain_accounting.py

Running the file alone gives 12 failures, all `PublicationDrainTimedOut: scanner alarm`. `test_cleanup_after_success_does_not_resurrect` is one of them. The file passes when an earlier test in the same process has already imported `sase.core.git_lock_facade`. Earlier triage showed 9 failed / 3 passed when the file ran cold and 12/12 passed when `sase.core.git_lock_facade` was preloaded before `pytest.main`. That is why the full suite usually passes, and why runs that start with this file, or put it first on an xdist worker, fail.

## Root cause

`test_scanner_timeout_unwinds_drain_and_leaves_request_queued` (added in 4356cffaa1, sase-1pt.6, 2026-10-30) monkeypatches the whole lookup:

    monkeypatch.setattr("sase.core.rust.require_rust_binding", lambda name: timeout_binding)

So every binding name raises `PublicationDrainTimedOut("scanner alarm")`. `src/sase/core/git_lock_facade.py:17` runs `from sase.core.rust import require_rust_binding` at module level. If the facade is first imported while that patch is active (during git-directory resolution inside the test), the facade keeps a reference to the patched lambda. Monkeypatch undo only restores `sase.core.rust.require_rust_binding`, so the facade's copy stays poisoned for the rest of the process. From then on, every git call in that process (`git_lock_retry_delays` -> `git_lock_wire_schema_version`) raises "scanner alarm" before reaching the intended scanner boundary.

## Fix direction

- In the test, patch only the scanner binding (the attachment-scan binding the test means to time out). Delegate every other name to the real `require_rust_binding`. Alternatively, patch the scanner call site directly.
- Optionally make `git_lock_facade` resolve `sase.core.rust.require_rust_binding` at call time, so a late first import can never capture a test double.
- Keep the scanner-timeout coverage and the `assert outcome.failure_scope == "repository"` assertion that sase-1r8.2 added.
- Add a regression check that runs the file cold, without `git_lock_facade` preloaded. For example, run the node first in a fresh interpreter, or assert that `git_lock_facade.require_rust_binding is sase.core.rust.require_rust_binding` after the test.

## History

This mechanism was recorded twice as a DISCOVERED ISSUE on epic sase-j7 (notes #91 and #93, from the sase-1qt and sase-1r8 landers), but nobody picked it up. sase-j7's phases all closed in August, before 4356cffaa1 introduced the defect, so that epic did not cause it and is not working on it. sase-xo is a separate, load-sensitive bounded-drain wall-clock flake in a different module.

It only passes when an earlier test already imported the facade.
